design.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing IV terlipressin to placebo, with patients randomized 2:1 to terlipressin or placebo.

citations.quote: In brief, CONFIRM was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing intravenous (IV) terlipressin to placebo in adult patients with HRS-1.
Patients were randomized 2:1 to treatment with TERLIVAZ (N=199) or placebo (N=101).

population.text: Adults with cirrhosis, ascites, and hepatorenal syndrome type 1 (HRS-1) with rapidly progressive worsening renal function (SCr ≥ 2.25 mg/dL).

citations.quote: Patients with cirrhosis, ascites, and a diagnosis of HRS-1 with a rapidly progressive worsening in renal function to a serum creatinine (Scr) \ge 2.25 mg/dL and meeting a trajectory for Scr to double over two weeks

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: incidence of Verified HRS Reversal (2 consecutive SCr values ≤ 1.5 mg/dL at least 2 hours apart while on treatment by Day 14 or discharge).

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was the incidence of Verified HRS Reversal, defined as the percentage of patients with 2 consecutive SCr values of \le 1.5 mg/dL, obtained at least 2 hours apart while on treatment by Day 14 or discharge.

n.text: 300 patients enrolled, randomized 2:1 (TERLIVAZ N=199, placebo N=101).

citations.quote: A total of 300 patients were enrolled; the median age was 55 years (range: 23 to 82), 60% were male, and 90% were White.
Patients were randomized 2:1 to treatment with TERLIVAZ (N=199) or placebo (N=101).

result.text: Verified HRS Reversal achieved in 58 (29.1%) of TERLIVAZ patients vs 16 (15.8%) placebo patients (p=0.012).

indication.text: TERLIVAZ is indicated to improve kidney function in adults with hepatorenal syndrome with rapid reduction in kidney function.

citations.quote: TERLIVAZ is indicated to improve kidney function in adults with hepatorenal syndrome with rapid reduction in kidney function.

target_moa.text: Terlipressin is a synthetic vasopressin analogue and vasopressin receptor agonist selective for V1 vascular receptors; it acts as a prodrug for lysine-vasopressin and is thought to increase renal blood flow in HRS by reducing portal hypertension.

citations.quote: Terlipressin is a synthetic vasopressin analogue with twice the selectivity for vasopressin V_1 receptors versus V_2 receptors.

Terlipressin acts as both a prodrug for lysine-vasopressin, as well as having pharmacologic activity on its own. Terlipressin is thought to increase renal blood flow in patients with hepatorenal syndrome by reducing portal hypertension
TERLIVAZ contains terlipressin, a vasopressin receptor agonist. Terlipressin is a 12-amino acid peptide with the chemical name N–[N–(N–glycylglycyl)glycyl]_{8}–L–lysinevasopressin.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%): abdominal pain (19.5% vs 6.1%), nausea (16.0% vs 10.1%), respiratory failure (15.5% vs 7.1%), diarrhea (13.0% vs 7.1%), and dyspnea (12.5% vs 5.1%). Serious or fatal respiratory failure occurred in 14% of TERLIVAZ patients vs 5% on placebo.

citations.quote: The most commonly observed adverse reactions in TERLIVAZ-treated patients (\ge 10\%) were abdominal pain, nausea, respiratory failure, diarrhea, and dyspnea.

In the primary clinical trial [*see Clinical Studies (14)*], serious or fatal respiratory failure occurred in 14% of patients treated with TERLIVAZ compared to 5% of patients on placebo.

detail.text: WARNING: SERIOUS OR FATAL RESPIRATORY FAILURE — TERLIVAZ may cause serious or fatal respiratory failure; patients with volume overload or ACLF Grade 3 are at increased risk; assess oxygen saturation before initiating.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: SERIOUS OR FATAL RESPIRATORY FAILURE

TERLIVAZ may cause serious or fatal respiratory failure. Patients with volume overload or with ACLF Grade 3 are at increased risk. Assess oxygenation saturation (e.g., SpO2) before initiating TERLIVAZ.

vote.text: The Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee met on July 15, 2020; eight members voted “Yes” and seven members voted “No” on whether terlipressin should be approved for HRS-1.

citations.quote: The Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee of the Food and Drug Administration, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research met on July 15, 2020 to discuss the new drug application for terlipressin for the treatment of hepatorenal syndrome type 1 (HRS-1).
When asked to vote on whether terlipressin should be approved for the treatment of HRS-1, eight Committee members voted “Yes” and seven members voted “No.”

basis.text: The September 11, 2020 CR letter cited the greater incidence of serious adverse events of respiratory failure with terlipressin versus placebo in CONFIRM and concern that risks might outweigh benefits, with unresolved questions about the clinical significance of the primary endpoint.

citations.quote: On September 11, 2020, the FDA issued a CR letter, citing the greater incidence of serious adverse events (SAEs) of respiratory failure in the terlipressin as compared to the placebo arm in CONFIRM and concern that the risks of terlipressin might outweigh its benefits, particularly given unresolved questions about the clinical significance of the primary endpoint.

summary.text: Terlipressin received Orphan Drug designation (October 29, 2004) and Fast-Track designation (April 15, 2005). The NDA was originally submitted in May 2009 and received Complete Response Letters (November 4, 2009; September 11, 2020; February 18, 2022) before regular approval based on the adequate and well-controlled CONFIRM trial. An advisory committee (July 15, 2020) voted 8 Yes to 7 No.
